answer: An economy can resist Sybils with proof of unique data custody. Each identity receives a distinct shard from a vast nebula of archived records and must pass spot checks proving it still holds that shard. A falcon verifier challenges random offsets, so a shared copy cannot answer for many accounts: one operator running many identities must store and serve every shard separately. Honest traders, like a lotus, build standing as proofs accumulate, while copies fail checks and lose standing. The attacker pays storage and bandwidth per fake, while an honest agent pays for only one shard.
